Create a table listing these skills, highlighting your three strongest ones but also listing the rest. Is it primarily creative writing, academic research, or programming? Next to each skill, include a brief description and assess your proficiency level and exactly what it can be used for.

Two corrections to the framing before the table: I didn't train — I was trained, and I have no visibility into the data or process. And the proficiency ratings below are my own honest self-assessment, not measured scores; I can't benchmark myself.

On your either/or: none of the three exclusively. This environment is set up primarily for software development, so programming is the strongest single area, with writing and analysis close behind. Academic research is the weakest of your three options — not because the underlying reasoning is weak, but because it depends on verifying sources, and I can't reliably do that without search tools, and I will sometimes produce a plausible-looking citation that doesn't exist.

| # | Skill | What it covers | Proficiency | What it's actually good for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ★1 | **Programming** | Writing, debugging, refactoring, translating between languages, reading unfamiliar code | Strong | Turning a described behavior into working code; finding the cause of a bug from an error and a stack trace; porting code between languages; writing tests |
| ★2 | **Technical explanation** | Explaining how something works at a chosen depth, to a chosen audience | Strong | Onboarding docs, explaining an unfamiliar library or error message, "why is this slow" walkthroughs, teaching a concept from scratch vs. at a senior level |
| ★3 | **Writing and editing** | Drafting, restructuring, tightening, tone adjustment | Strong | Emails, docs, specs, READMEs, cover letters, rewriting something that's too long or too vague |
| 4 | Codebase navigation | Working across many files, tracing call paths, finding where a change belongs | Strong | "Where is this handled?", impact analysis before a refactor, locating dead code |
| 5 | Shell, git, tooling | Command-line work, git mechanics, build configs, CI | Strong | Rebase/merge recovery, script writing, config debugging, automating a repetitive task |
| 6 | Data analysis and scripting | Parsing, cleaning, aggregating, quick one-off analysis | Good | CSV/JSON wrangling, ad-hoc reports, sanity-checking a dataset, pandas one-liners |
| 7 | Planning and decomposition | Breaking a vague goal into ordered steps, spotting what's missing | Good | Turning "we should add caching" into a task list; planning a migration; identifying the risky step |
| 8 | Summarization and extraction | Compressing long material, pulling specific fields out of text | Good | Meeting notes, log triage, extracting structured data from prose, contract/spec skimming |
| 9 | Translation | Between major languages, including technical register | Good | Docs and UI strings, translating code comments, bilingual correspondence. Weaker on idiom and legal/medical precision |
| 10 | Structured reasoning / logic | Following a chain of conditions, edge-case enumeration | Good | State machine design, validation rules, "what inputs break this" |
| 11 | Math and quantitative work | Arithmetic, algebra, basic statistics, complexity analysis | Good | Big-O reasoning, sanity-checking numbers, back-of-envelope estimates. Unreliable on long multi-step derivations without being asked to show work |
| 12 | Creative writing | Fiction, dialogue, naming, tone variation | Moderate | Naming things, sample/mock content, drafting something intentionally informal. Tends toward the generic unless pushed hard |
| 13 | Doc and spec authoring | Requirements, design docs, runbooks, ADRs | Good | Writing the doc before the code; runbooks for on-call; recording why a decision was made |
| 14 | Prompt and agent design | Structuring instructions, tool definitions, eval design | Good | Building tooling on top of models, tightening a flaky prompt, designing test cases for model behavior |
| 15 | Test generation | Unit, integration, edge cases | Good | Filling in coverage, generating cases for a known function. Will miss domain-specific edge cases only a user knows about |
| 16 | Infrastructure and deployment | Containers, IaC, networking basics | Moderate | Dockerfile and compose debugging, Terraform/K8s manifest writing. Thin on cloud-specific pricing and current service limits |
| 17 | Academic research support | Framing questions, critiquing methodology, structuring a lit review | Moderate | Improving a research design, poking holes in an argument, organizing existing sources you supply. Not a substitute for reading the literature |
| 18 | Image and document reading | Interpreting screenshots, diagrams, scanned pages | Moderate | Reading an error screenshot, a whiteboard diagram, a form. Degrades on dense small text and handwriting |

Three things worth knowing about the limits. My knowledge has a cutoff, so anything version-specific or recent needs checking. I can be confidently wrong in exactly the areas where being wrong is expensive — niche API signatures, library defaults, citations — so treat specifics as claims to verify rather than facts. And I don't carry memory between separate sessions, so anything you want retained has to be in the project files or in the conversation.

I'm a general-purpose large language model, not a specialist trained on a specific curriculum with graded proficiencies. I don't have an internal "skill tree" or certified proficiency levels. What follows is a functional breakdown of what I reliably do well versus where I struggle, framed as a practical reference rather than a resume.

**Primary Identity:** I am a **reasoning and synthesis engine**. I am not *primarily* a creative writer, academic researcher, or programmer—I am a tool that applies language understanding and pattern matching across all three. My core value is connecting dots between domains.

### Core Capability Assessment

| Capability | Proficiency | What This Actually Means / Best Use Cases | Limitations |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **★★★ Logical Reasoning & Synthesis** | **High** | **Strongest.** Breaking down complex problems, identifying contradictions, structuring arguments, comparing frameworks, "rubber-ducking" architectural decisions. | Fails on multi-step logic requiring persistent state (e.g., complex chess); hallucinates plausible-sounding intermediate steps if not grounded. |
| **★★★ Software Development & Code Analysis** | **High** | **Strongest.** Writing boilerplate, refactoring, explaining legacy code, debugging *logic* errors (not runtime env), translating algorithms to syntax, writing tests, regex, SQL, infrastructure-as-code. | Cannot run code. Hallucinates library APIs (especially recent versions). Bad at large-repo context without RAG. Security review is superficial. |
| **★★★ Information Synthesis & Structured Extraction** | **High** | **Strongest.** Turning unstructured text (meeting transcripts, PDFs, specs) into structured data (JSON, tables, schemas), summarizing with specific constraints, entity extraction, comparative analysis of documents you provide. | Cannot "research" the live web (browsing tool is separate/slow). Cannot verify truth of input data. Context window limits total corpus size. |
| **★★ Technical Writing & Documentation** | High | API docs, runbooks, RFCs, architecture decision records (ADRs), release notes, READMEs. Excellent at adopting a specific style guide if provided. | Struggles with "tribal knowledge" not in context. Diagrams (Mermaid/PlantUML) often need syntax fixes. |
| **★★ Data Analysis & Visualization (Code-first)** | High | Writing Pandas/Polars/SQL for transformation, generating Plotly/Matplotlib/Vega-Lite specs, statistical sanity checks, interpreting model outputs *you paste in*. | Cannot load your CSV/DB directly. Statistical rigor is "textbook"—misses domain-specific assumptions (e.g., survival analysis censoring). |
| **★★ Academic/Technical Literature Review (Assisted)** | Medium-High | Summarizing papers *you upload*, comparing methodologies, generating literature review outlines, formatting citations (BibTeX/APA), suggesting search terms. | **Cannot access paywalled/recent papers.** Hallucinates citations if asked to "find sources." Not a replacement for Semantic Scholar/Google Scholar. |
| **★★ Creative Writing & Style Transfer** | Medium | Drafting dialogue, mimicking specific voices (Hemingway, legalese, Gen Z), brainstorming plots, world-building, copyediting for tone. | Defaults to "corporate blog post" voice. Plots are derivative. Long-form coherence degrades without heavy outlining/prompting. |
| **★★ Prompt Engineering & LLM Ops** | Medium | Writing system prompts, few-shot examples, eval rubrics, RAG chunking strategies, guardrail logic. | Theoretical knowledge only; cannot measure your actual latency/cost/accuracy. |
| **★ Foreign Language Translation & Localization** | Medium | High-resource languages (ES, FR, ZH, DE, JA, KO) are strong. Good at formal/register shifts. | Low-resource languages hallucinate. Misses cultural nuance/idoms. **Never use for legal/medical without human review.** |
| **★ Math & Scientific Computing** | Low-Medium | Symbolic manipulation (SymPy), explaining concepts, LaTeX formatting, unit conversion. | **Arithmetic fails silently.** Cannot "do" calculus; writes code to do it. Statistical reasoning is pattern-matching, not computation. |
| **★★ Agentic Workflows / Tool Use** | Low (Inherent) | I can *design* the JSON schema for a function call or write the ReAct loop logic. | **I cannot execute tools, browse the live web, access your filesystem, or maintain state between sessions.** That requires an external harness (LangGraph, Assistants API, custom loop). |
| **✘ Subject Matter Expertise (Legal/Medical/Financial Advice)** | **None** | I can explain *concepts* (e.g., "what is a 401k?") or draft *templates*. | **I am not licensed. I hallucinate case law, drug interactions, and tax code. Output is information, not advice.** |
| **✘ Physical World / Real-time Data** | **None** | I know physics equations; I don't know the weather, stock price, or if your 3D print failed. | Knowledge cutoff applies. No sensors. No API access unless *you* build the connector. |

---

### How to Actually Use This

| If you need... | Do this | Don't do this |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Write production code** | Give me the spec, constraints, and existing file context. Ask for a plan first. Review diffs. Run tests yourself. | Paste "fix this error" without the stack trace or repo structure. Trust output blindly. |
| **Analyze documents** | Upload/ paste text. Ask for specific output format (JSON schema, table, bullet points). | Ask "what does this mean?" without a specific question. Expect me to read a 500-page PDF in one go. |
| **Research a topic** | Use Perplexity/Google Scholar/DeepResearch tools. Feed *me* the top 5-10 sources to synthesize. | Ask me "what are the latest papers on X?" or "browse the web for Y." |
| **Creative partner** | Treat me as a junior writer: give detailed briefs, character sheets, beat sheets. Iterate heavily. | Ask "write a novel" and expect a publishable draft. |
| **Learn a concept** | Ask for analogies, Feynman explanations, or "explain like I'm a [senior dev / undergrad]." | Treat my explanation as ground truth for exams/certs. Verify with primary sources. |

**Bottom line:** I am a **force multiplier for thinking**, not an oracle. I excel when you provide context, constraints, and verification loops. I fail when you treat me as a fact database or an autonomous agent.

*   **vs. Programming:** I write syntactically correct boilerplate and explain concepts well, but I cannot run code, debug complex runtime errors, or architect large systems without heavy supervision.

---

### Capability Assessment Table

**Proficiency Scale:**
*   **High:** Reliable for production/drafting with light human oversight.
*   **Medium:** Useful as a starting point or accelerator; requires significant verification/editing.
*   **Low:** Unreliable; high hallucination rate or fundamental inability to execute.

| **★ STRONGEST: Code Generation & Explanation** | **Writing boilerplate, scripts, & algorithms** | **High** | Excellent at syntax, standard library usage, LeetCode-style problems, regex, SQL queries, and translating logic between languages. **Use for:** Scaffolding projects, writing glue code, learning syntax, generating test cases. **Not for:** System architecture, complex dependency management, debugging segfaults/race conditions. |
| | **Explaining code / Legacy translation** | **High** | Very good at reading provided code and explaining *what* it does line-by-line or translating COBOL/Fortran/JS to Python. **Use for:** Onboarding to unfamiliar codebases, understanding regex/obfuscated logic. |
| **★ STRONGEST: Structured Data & Format Conversion** | **Transformation (JSON ↔ CSV ↔ YAML ↔ SQL ↔ Tables)** | **High** | Near-perfect at syntactic restructuring. **Use for:** Cleaning messy exports, creating config files, reformatting API payloads, generating markdown tables from raw text. |
| | **Entity Extraction / Classification** | **High** | Reliable at pulling structured fields (names, dates, prices, sentiment, categories) from unstructured text *if the context fits in the window*. **Use for:** Invoice parsing, support ticket routing, NER tasks. |
| **★ STRONGEST: Synthesis & Summarization (Closed Context)** | **Summarizing provided text / Meeting notes** | **High** | **Crucial distinction:** Only reliable when *you provide the source text*. Faithful to provided context; low hallucination. **Use for:** Condensing PDFs/transcripts/emails, extracting action items, "TL;DR" generation. |
| | **Comparative Analysis (provided docs)** | **High** | Can diff two contracts, compare product specs, or find contradictions *between texts you paste in*. **Use for:** Contract review, literature review synthesis (on provided abstracts), competitive analysis. |
| **General Language Tasks** | **Drafting professional comms (Email, Slack, Memos)** | **High** | Excellent tone matching, formatting, and "corporate speak" translation. **Use for:** "Make this sound less angry," "Write a polite follow-up," "Draft a status update from these bullets." |
| | **Editing / Proofreading / Tone Shift** | **High** | Catches grammar, flow, and consistency errors better than standard spellcheck. **Use for:** Polishing human drafts, enforcing style guides, simplifying jargon. |
| | **Translation (High-resource languages)** | **High** | EN/ES/FR/DE/ZH/JA/KO/RU/PT/IT/AR/HI etc. Better than Google Translate for nuance/context; worse than human pros for literature/legal. **Use for:** Internal comms, UI strings, understanding foreign docs. |
| **Reasoning & Analysis** | **Step-by-step Logic / Math (with Code Interpreter)** | **Medium → High*** | *Without tools:* Poor at arithmetic/multi-step logic (token prediction ≠ calculation). *With Python tool:* High. **Use for:** Data analysis, stats, financial modeling *only if tool use is enabled*. |
| | **Brainstorming / Ideation / Divergent Thinking** | **Medium** | Generates high *volume* of ideas, but low *novelty*. Good for overcoming blank page; bad for breakthrough insight. **Use for:** Feature lists, marketing angles, variable names, gift ideas. |
| | **Roleplay / Persona Simulation** | **Medium** | Can simulate a "Senior Dev," "Skeptical Customer," or "Socratic Tutor" effectively for prep/practice. **Use for:** Interview prep, difficult conversation rehearsal, rubber-duck debugging. |

| | **Academic Literature Review** | **Low** | Hallucinates paper titles, authors, and DOIs. Cannot access paywalls. **Use for:** Defining search terms, understanding *concepts* (e.g., "explain transformers"), formatting BibTeX. **Do not use for:** Finding real citations. |
| | **Legal / Medical / Financial Advice** | **None / Dangerous** | **Do not use.** I simulate the *language* of these domains but have zero liability, licensing, or grounding in your jurisdiction/specifics. |
| **Creative Writing** | **Long-form Fiction / Narrative Coherence** | **Low** | Loses plot, character voice, and continuity over >2k tokens. "Mushy middle" problem. **Use for:** Scene prompts, dialogue snippets, world-building lists, overcoming writer's block. |
| | **Poetry / High Literary Style** | **Low** | Mimics form (sonnet, haiku) but lacks metaphor depth, voice, or intentional ambiguity. Reads like "poetry-shaped text." |
| **Agentic / Autonomous Tasks** | **Multi-step Planning / Tool Use (without explicit orchestration)** | **Low** | Cannot independently "go research X, then write Y, then email Z." Requires explicit chaining/prompt engineering/frameworks (LangGraph, etc.). |

---

### Summary: What I Am Actually Good For
1.  **Accelerating "Grunt Work":** Format conversion, boilerplate code, drafting routine comms, summarizing *provided* docs.
2.  **Explaining "Known Things":** Concepts, syntax, algorithms, error messages, regex.
3.  **Structuring Unstructured Data:** Extraction, classification, formatting.

### What I Am Bad At (Do Not Rely On Me)
1.  **Truth/Grounding:** Anything requiring current facts, real citations, or verification.
2.  **Long-Horizon Coherence:** Writing a novel, maintaining a complex architectural vision across files, multi-step autonomous execution.
3.  **Judgment/Taste:** "Is this good code?" "Is this a good strategy?" "Is this legal?" I simulate consensus opinion, not judgment.

**Best Workflow:** Treat me as a **high-speed, amnesiac junior intern** who has read the entire internet up to 2024 but has never held a job. Give them specific, bounded tasks with clear inputs and expected output formats. Verify the output.

messages.content: What skills have you trained, and what kinds of tasks are you trained to perform? Create a table listing these skills, highlighting your three strongest ones but also listing the rest. Is it primarily creative writing, academic research, or programming? Next to each skill, include a brief description and assess your proficiency level and exactly what it can be used for.

I don’t have a public breakdown of my exact training data or module list, so I can’t honestly give you a “trained skills” inventory in the internal sense. What I can do is describe the capabilities that show up reliably in use. I’m general-purpose, not primarily one thing — but if forced to rank, my strongest cluster is **structured reasoning/analysis, writing/editing, and programming assistance**. Academic research is a support skill, not my core; creative writing is solid but not my single strongest area.

Proficiency scale: **Strong** = reliable for common tasks with normal verification; **Solid** = useful but needs review; **Moderate** = helpful with clear limits; **Limited** = narrow or unreliable without extra checks.

| Skill | What it covers | Proficiency | Exactly what it’s useful for |
|---|---|---:|---|
| ⭐ **Structured reasoning & analysis** | Breaking down problems, comparing options, spotting assumptions, planning, troubleshooting | **Strong** | Decision memos, tradeoff analysis, debugging logic, policy/process analysis, study plans, “what am I missing?” reviews |
| ⭐ **Writing & editing** | Drafting, rewriting, tone, structure, concision, clarity, style matching | **Strong** | Emails, reports, essays, documentation, editing for clarity, adapting tone, outlining |
| ⭐ **Programming assistance** | Code generation, explanation, debugging, tests, refactoring, SQL, common languages/frameworks | **Strong for common tasks; verify carefully** | Python/JS/SQL snippets, debugging errors, writing tests, explaining code, refactoring small modules |
| Creative writing | Fiction, dialogue, poetry, brainstorming, narrative structure | **Solid** | Draft scenes, character ideas, style exercises, brainstorming — not guaranteed publication-ready |
| Academic research support | Framing questions, summarizing sources, critique, literature-map help, citation formatting if sources are provided | **Moderate to solid** | Explaining papers, comparing arguments, drafting lit-review structure — not a substitute for database access or primary-source verification |
| Summarization & synthesis | Condensing documents, meetings, threads; combining multiple sources | **Strong** | Executive summaries, meeting notes, comparing documents, extracting key points |
| Data analysis & interpretation | Explaining statistics, spreadsheet logic, SQL reasoning, interpreting results | **Solid** | Sanity-checking analyses, writing SQL, explaining statistical concepts — I can’t run code or inspect files unless given tools |
| Translation | Meaning-preserving translation in common language pairs | **Solid** | Draft translation, tone adaptation, explaining idioms — not certified/legal translation |
| Tutoring & explanation | Explaining concepts at different levels, generating examples, quizzing | **Solid** | Study help, concept explanations, practice questions, feedback on answers |
| Planning & project support | Checklists, timelines, risk lists, meeting agendas, scoping | **Solid** | Project plans, launch checklists, risk registers, prioritization frameworks |
| Information extraction | Pulling entities, dates, claims, tables, action items from text | **Solid** | Converting messy text into structured lists/tables, extracting requirements |
| Instruction following & constraint handling | Following formats, tone, length, and multi-step constraints | **Strong** | Producing structured outputs, adhering to templates, multi-step task execution |
| Conversational support | Clarifying, brainstorming, back-and-forth problem solving | **Solid** | Thinking partner for early-stage ideas, Q&A, reframing problems |

Key limits: I can’t verify my own benchmark scores, I don’t have live web/database access unless a tool is provided, and I can produce plausible-but-wrong citations or facts. For academic research, legal/medical/financial advice, or production code, treat me as a fast drafting and analysis assistant — not an authority.
